title: A Cover for the Contact
premise: Ines Montrose, a disgraced intelligence analyst, discovers the safe house he's hidden in for five years has been listed online — complete with interior photos that expose his life in hiding. The listing is bait: someone inside the agencies that burned him wants him found before he can testify to a tribunal about a sanctioned operation that killed civilians. Hunted by an assassin named Veyra and blocked by three governments rewriting the record, Ines must reconstruct his own redacted memory of that night. He ends by trading himself to Veyra in exchange for the evidence reaching the tribunal, choosing justice outside every system that failed him.
about_author: Rosalind Nystrom is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing declassified files before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse in northern Sweden, where she insists the best thrillers are about paperwork.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ines, scrolling property sites out of boredom, finds the safe house listed with photos of his own kitchen, his own books, a coffee cup on the table. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: cold dread — five years of invisibility collapsing in a single webpage.

chapters.title: Rules That Move
chapters.summary: Ines reviews his handler's last message and realizes the extraction protocol changed twice without notice; the agency that promised protection no longer exists under that name. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: bitter recognition that the rules were never meant to protect him.

chapters.title: Veyra Signs the Guestbook
chapters.summary: A woman posing as a buyer tours the house while Ines watches from the attic crawlspace; she leaves a calling card in the doorframe — a professional's courtesy. POV: alternating Ines and Veyra. Emotional beat: hunter and prey acknowledging each other.

chapters.title: What the Photos Sold
chapters.summary: Ines studies the listing photos frame by frame and realizes they were staged to show him specific objects — including a file box he thought was destroyed. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose; someone wants him to run toward something.

chapters.title: The Burned Analyst's Club
chapters.summary: Ines contacts Odile Ferrant, a former colleague also discarded by the system, who agrees to help if he tells her what really happened at Kestrel Station. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: wary belonging between two people the state erased.

chapters.title: Redacted Night
chapters.summary: Ines attempts to reconstruct the Kestrel Station incident from fragments and hits a wall of chemically blurred memory — he was there, but he can't prove what he saw. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief over a self he cannot fully access.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Odile reveals all three governments signed a joint suppression order; the truth exists only in Ines's head and one physical archive. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: vertigo at the scale of the cover-up.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ines traces the real estate listing to a shell company and finds it funded by the same office that ordered the suppression. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: rage hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ines learning tradecraft, told invisibility means having nothing worth taking — a lesson the listing just falsified. POV: Ines (past). Emotional beat: tenderness for his former self, now ironic.

chapters.title: Veyra's Contract
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV: her employer changed the terms mid-contract — not kill, retrieve alive — and she begins questioning who actually hired her. POV: Veyra. Emotional beat: a professional's unease turning into doubt.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Ines and Odile move toward the archive in Rotterdam using smuggler routes; a checkpoint nearly catches them when Ines's face appears on a watchlist updated hours earlier. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension, first real trust between them.

chapters.title: The Archive Keeper
chapters.summary: They meet Bram, an ex-archivist who guards off-book records; he confirms the Kestrel file exists but requires something in trade — Ines's testimony, recorded. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: memory as currency; belonging among keepers of inconvenient truths.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Ines enters the archive stacks while Odile runs interference; he finds the file — and finds it already half-empty, pages surgically removed. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: hope curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Who Took the Pages
chapters.summary: Bram's logs show the pages were removed three years ago — by someone with Ines's access codes, during the window he can't remember. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: horror that the traitor may be himself.

chapters.title: Chemical Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Odile identifies the memory-blurring drug used on Ines and its withdrawal window; recovery will be brutal and might not work. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: fierce loyalty offered without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Coming Back
chapters.summary: Ines endures detox and the memories return in shards: he removed the pages himself, on orders, then chose to forget rather than live as their keeper. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: devastating self-reckoning; he was both victim and instrument.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Ines contacts Veyra directly and offers a deal: himself, delivered, in exchange for her employer's name and safe passage for the reconstructed testimony. POV: Veyra. Emotional beat: two professionals negotiating across the line between them.

chapters.title: The Handover
chapters.summary: The exchange happens at a canal warehouse; Veyra takes him in, but Odile has already seeded copies of the testimony through three independent channels. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: sacrifice made calmly, almost tenderly.

chapters.title: Employer Revealed
chapters.summary: In custody, Ines learns his original handler orchestrated everything — the burn, the forgetting, the listing — to flush out the last living witness before a treaty signing. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: betrayal complete, clarity absolute.

chapters.title: Tribunal Day
chapters.summary: Copies reach the tribunal despite a blackout attempt; Veyra, doubting her contract, releases Ines rather than deliver him to silencing. POV: Veyra. Emotional beat: justice chosen outside the law, by the law's own weapon.

chapters.title: Public Record
chapters.summary: The Kestrel testimony enters the record; governments scramble, careers fall, and Ines watches from a courtroom gallery as a stranger reads his words aloud. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet vindication that costs him everything but his name.

chapters.title: A New Address
chapters.summary: Months later, Ines buys a small house openly, under his own name, and hangs the listing photo of the old safe house framed on the wall. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: belonging finally chosen, not assigned — visibility as victory.
